message.content:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:

   The session covered several major work-streams, most recently a large **Ticket-based investigation tracking feature** for the `cmp-mcp` admin GUI, followed by extensive UI iteration on that feature's Dashboard presentation, and finally a **brand-new per-event commenting system**.

   Verbatim key user requests, in order:
   - "test done?" / "why task still running" — process hygiene checks (resolved: killed hung pytest processes from a report-gating test that hung waiting for approval).
   - The big ticket-feature request (paraphrased across several messages): redesign the Dashboard to show "Ticket" (an investigation, ongoing/completed-success/completed-failed), with Logs page able to show one ticket's logs at a time via selection. Explicit answers to my clarifying questions: ticket_id should be "an outer layer that doesn't strictly depend on which implementation of an MCP" — should work automatically without the model needing to pass it as an argument, tied to a Claude Code session ("each investigation is created from a session... session ID will be passed into... as the ticket ID and that will remain").
   - A detailed voice-message specifying the ticket state machine verbatim: "This is our ticket state: Investigating, Planned, Resolving (or you make another name), In Review, Completed, Escalated. Investigating: is when a new log error detected, newly issued. Planned: is when the plan finished, but if the user make comment on the plan, then the state goes back to investigating until plan finished. Resolving...: is when the plan is accepted and being fixed. In Review: is when the resolved and output a report waiting to be accept (make the report approval just like plan, can comment on it as well). if comment, then back to Resolving...Completed: When it is resolved and report accepted. Escalated: When report is denied or the ticket trigger notify admin, escalated. Display smart, whatever more important place first (for e.g. those completed place at the end. And also have button to filter which state want to see."
   - Reference image (Sprint Timeline + Kanban "All Tasks" board) with instruction: "make the progress bar and the comment. But do not make columns like that." — wanted card-based UI inspired by the reference but NOT literal side-by-side kanban columns.
   - First redesign-feedback message (verbatim, paraphrased slightly for length): wanted no stat-card number summaries (numbers go on filter buttons instead), filter should be "more elegant" not plain buttons and should show numbers, default (nothing clicked) should show all tickets, clicking one filters to just that state, no outer panel/card wrapper (match reference image), no badge for state/completion, "make the card looks better," replace the horizontal color line with "the most recent tool or action" (e.g. "plan approved", "plan done"), replace the badge with "a color icon that indicate the state of the ticket," and delete confirmation must be "a custom one that pops up in the center of the screen" not a "default notification."
   - Correction message (verbatim): "No. It's supposed to be, um, grid like. Not that one ticket span the full horizon like this. My... what I mean goes down vertical is that if you on the old ticket mode, there'll be late subsections, meaning that you can see the... it's still on, like, the prioritize... priority order. So you wanna see subsections of the escalated and review resolving plan investigating and complete? all in that. Yeah. and each. And, also, I don't want a... okay. That's it. And the same goes for escalated and interview. One more thing is that in the log, when I want to filter of a... I I mean, in the locks, I should be able to see the session ID. way we don't display assassin ID, so we say it as ticket ID. Yeah." — meaning: cards should be in a responsive GRID (multi-column) within per-state SUBSECTIONS (stacked vertically in priority order), not one flat vertical list of full-width cards; and the Logs page (specifically the event detail) should show the ticket's identifying number, labeled "Ticket ID" (not the raw session_id UUID).
   - Mid-turn: "and bring back the comment count and deep link" — restore the comment_count display and the "View logs" deep-link affordance on ticket cards, which had been dropped in the prior redesign pass.
   - Mid-turn: "I dont want just red and green, display more vibrant colors in the icons and the most recent action/tool display dont need to be in the same color background, it looks ugly." — use more/more-vibrant distinct colors per state (not just red/green, and not two states sharing the same color), and stop tinting the "most recent action" caption strip with the state color.
   - Mid-turn: "and use filled icon" — switch the ticket-state icons to heroicons' solid/filled variant instead of outline.
   - Mid-turn, introducing a wholly new feature (verbatim): "The comment here is not the comment at the plan or report when review, they are actual comment, new thing introduce into our system. Is that the admin are able to make comment at each step/action (little icon at the right of the action/tool log that when click onto, a popup to see list of comments. When reading tools collapsed, comments are also grouped to display at the right. Display the comment icon (if has comment) along with the number of comment there (at the right)." — a genuinely new, general-purpose per-event commenting system, distinct from the existing plan/report "request changes" comment mechanism.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - MCP (Model Context Protocol): tools, resources (`ReadMcpResourceTool`, `ListMcpResourcesTool`), prompts (only invocable as user slash commands, never by an agent mid-skill).
   - `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` environment variable — empirically verified real, stable per-conversation, and propagates through `.mcp.json`'s exact spawn command (`uv --directory cmp-mcp run python -m mcp_servers.<server>.main`) to every MCP server subprocess for that session. This is the foundation of the whole ticket-attribution mechanism — verified via `uv run python -c "import os; print(os.environ.get('CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID'))"` matching the Bash tool's own env.
   - Windows `SO_REUSEADDR` quirk: allows multiple processes to simultaneously bind the same TCP port, causing "phantom" stale server instances to keep answering requests even after a supposed restart — hit repeatedly with both the mock CMP server and the admin_gui backend; fixed each time by explicitly enumerating `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='python.exe'"` and killing every matching PID before starting exactly one fresh instance.
   - SQLite schema migration pattern in this project (`mcp_servers/shared/db.py`): a `_SCHEMA` string of `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`/`CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` run via `executescript`, followed by explicit `_migrate_*_columns(conn)` functions using `PRAGMA table_info` + `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` for backward-compatible column additions to pre-existing DBs — critical subtlety: a new index referencing a migrated-in column must live *inside* the migration function, never in `_SCHEMA`, since `_SCHEMA` runs first via `executescript` and would fail "no such column" on a pre-existing DB.
   - `instrument_dispatch` (`mcp_servers/shared/telemetry.py`) — the single chokepoint every dispatch path (tool calls across all 3 servers + resource reads) funnels through; this is where ticket attribution is injected generically, with zero changes needed to any of the ~150 generated tool schemas.
   - Ticket state machine: `investigating → planned → resolving → in_review → completed`, with `escalated` reachable from a flat plan/report denial or `notify_admin` running, implemented in new `mcp_servers/shared/tickets.py`.
   - FastAPI + `TestClient` for backend testing; `sqlite3.Row` row factory; correlated SQL subqueries for computed fields (`comment_count`, `event_count`, `latest_event_name/status/ts`).
   - Astryx design system components: `Card`, `Badge` (`BadgeVariant` type: neutral/success/warning/error/blue/orange/purple/cyan/pink/yellow/teal/gray), `Dialog`/`DialogHeader`/`Layout`/`LayoutContent` (modal pattern), `Selector` (supports `SelectorOptionData = {value, label, ...}` object options, not just bare strings), `TextArea`, `Button` (`variant`: primary/secondary/destructive/ghost; `isIconOnly`), `Link`, `HStack`/`VStack`, `Text` (`weight: 'normal'|'medium'|'semibold'|'bold'`, NOT `'regular'`).
   - CSS custom properties confirmed to exist (grepped from compiled Astryx dist): `--color-icon-{blue,purple,orange,green,red,cyan,pink,yellow,teal,gray,accent,disabled,primary,secondary}`, `--color-background-{blue,purple,orange,green,red,cyan,pink,yellow,teal,gray,muted,card,surface,body,error,inverted,popover}`.
   - `react-router-dom`'s `useSearchParams`/`useNavigate` for deep-linking (`/logs?ticket={id}`).
   - `@heroicons/react/24/outline` vs `@heroicons/react/24/solid` — switched ticket-state icons to solid per explicit request, kept utility icons (trash, chat bubble) as outline.
   - oxlint warnings: `react(set-state-in-effect)` is an accepted, pre-existing pattern throughout this codebase for data-fetch-on-mount components; new occurrences following the same convention are not treated as regressions.

3. Files and Code Sections:

   **Backend — DB schema**
   - `mcp_servers/shared/db.py`
     - Added `tickets` table: `id, session_id (UNIQUE), title, resource_id, state DEFAULT 'investigating', created_at, closed_at` + indexes `idx_tickets_session_id`, `idx_tickets_state`.
     - Added `comments` table: `id, event_id, text, created_at` + index `idx_comments_event_id`.
     - `_migrate_events_columns` extended to add `events.ticket_id INTEGER` (nullable, no FK) and create `idx_events_ticket_id` *inside* the migration function (not `_SCHEMA`), matching the pre-existing `action` column's migration pattern.

   **Backend — new `mcp_servers/shared/tickets.py`** (full module, final state)
     - `current_session_id()` — reads `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` env var.
     - `current_ticket_id(conn=None)` — looks up the open ticket for the current session; wrapped in `try/except (OSError, sqlite3.Error)` returning `None` on failure (fixed a real regression where a broken DB sink crashed `instrument_dispatch`); calls `db.ensure_schema()` first (fixed a real "no such table: tickets" bug on fresh DBs).
     - `open_ticket(title)` — idempotent per session (`INSERT ... ON` no-op via existing-row check first); does NOT swallow errors (primary explicit action, should surface failures); calls `db.ensure_schema()`.
     - `backfill_resource_id(ticket_id, resource_id)` — fills `tickets.resource_id` once, never overwrites; best-effort (wrapped try/except).
     - `_set_state`, `_close`, `_bump_if` — trivial UPDATE helpers, all wrapped in try/except + `db.ensure_schema()`.
     - `on_pending(ticket_id, name)` — `submit_investigation_report` going pending → ticket state `in_review`.
     - `on_dispatched(ticket_id, name, requires_approval)` — bumps `planned`→`resolving` on first real action dispatch, skipping the 3 lifecycle tools (`_LIFECYCLE_TOOLS = {"submit_investigation_plan", "submit_investigation_report", "notify_admin"}`).
     - `on_decision(ticket_id, name, decision)` — full transition matrix: plan approved→planned; plan changes_requested→investigating; plan denied→escalated(closed); report approved→completed(closed); report changes_requested→resolving; report denied→escalated(closed); notify_admin approved→escalated(closed).

   **Backend — `mcp_servers/shared/telemetry.py`**
     - `log_event`/`log_pending_event` gained `ticket_id: int | None = None` param, added to INSERT.
     - `instrument_dispatch`: computes `ticket_id = tickets.current_ticket_id()` up front; calls `tickets.on_pending(ticket_id, name)` right after creating a pending row; calls `tickets.on_dispatched(ticket_id, name, requires_approval)` right before dispatching; **critical fix**: re-checks `ticket_id = tickets.current_ticket_id()` again right before the final `log_event` call if it was `None`, so `start_investigate`'s own event correctly attributes to the ticket it just created (verified live: `start_investigate` event now shows `ticket_id: 1` instead of `None`).

   **Backend — `mcp_servers/cmp_admin_mcp/investigation_reporting.py`**
     - Added `_START_INVESTIGATE_INPUT_SCHEMA`, `run_start_investigate` (calls `tickets.open_ticket`), `build_start_investigate_tool()` (not gated, `idempotentHint=True`).
     - `run_submit_investigation_plan` now calls `tickets.backfill_resource_id(tickets.current_ticket_id(), arguments.get("resource_id"))`.
     - `build_submit_investigation_report_tool()` — flipped to `requires_approval=True` (was previously ungated); description text rewritten to describe the gated behavior.
     - Module docstring and `__all__` updated to include the three tools.

   **Backend — `mcp_servers/cmp_admin_mcp/main.py`** — registered `build_start_investigate_tool()` in `extra_tools=[...]`.

   **Backend — `admin_gui/backend/routers/events.py`** (current full relevant state)
     - `EventOut` gained `ticket_id: int | None` and `comment_count: int`.
     - New `_EVENTS_SELECT` constant: `"SELECT events.*, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM comments WHERE comments.event_id = events.id) AS comment_count FROM events"` — used by both `list_events` (replacing `SELECT * FROM events {where}`) and `_event_stream` (replacing its raw `SELECT * FROM events WHERE...`), with all bare column references in WHERE clauses left unprefixed (still valid since only one table in FROM).
     - `list_events` gained a `ticket_id: str | None` query param (`"unassigned"` sentinel for `IS NULL`, else parsed int).
     - `_decide_event` and `request_changes_event` now select `status, name, ticket_id` and call `tickets.on_decision(row["ticket_id"], row["name"], new_status_or_"changes_requested")` after updating.
     - New `CommentOut(BaseModel)`: `id, event_id, text, created_at`; `CommentCreate(BaseModel)`: `text: str`; `_row_to_comment`.
     - New endpoints: `GET /{event_id}/comments` (404 if event unknown) and `POST /{event_id}/comments` (body `{text}`, strips/validates non-empty → 400, 404 if event unknown) — both appended just before `__all__ = ["router"]`.

   **Backend — new `admin_gui/backend/routers/tickets.py`** (full file, final state)
     - `TicketOut`: `id, session_id, title, resource_id, state, created_at, closed_at, event_count, comment_count, latest_event_name, latest_event_status, latest_event_ts`.
     - `_COMMENT_EVENT_NAMES = ("submit_investigation_plan", "submit_investigation_report")`, `_COMMENT_NAME_PLACEHOLDERS` for parameterized `IN (?, ?)`.
     - `_LIST_SQL` — correlated subqueries for `event_count`, `comment_count` (ticket-level, counting `changes_requested` decisions on plan/report — explicitly NOT the same as the new per-event comments system), and `latest_event_name/status/ts` (each `ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1`).
     - `GET ""` (list, newest first), `GET "/{ticket_id}"` (404 if missing), `DELETE "/{ticket_id}"` — soft delete: `UPDATE events SET ticket_id = NULL WHERE ticket_id = ?` then `DELETE FROM tickets`, returns `{"detached_events": N}`.
     - Wired into `admin_gui/backend/app.py`'s router import tuple and `app.include_router(tickets.router, prefix="/api")`.

   **Skill — `.claude/skills/investigate-incident/SKILL.md`**
     - Step 1: added leading instruction to call `start_investigate` first with `title` = user's original request; explicitly states nothing else changes because of it.
     - Step 9 rewritten: report is now gated exactly like the plan (Step 5), with the same three-outcome handling (approved=done; denied-with-comment=go do more work then resubmit; denied-flat=escalate via `notify_admin`, same as Step 8).

   **Frontend — `admin_gui/frontend/src/lib/api.ts`**
     - `EventOut` gained `ticket_id: number | null` and `comment_count: number`.
     - New `TicketOut` interface (matches backend `TicketOut` exactly, including `latest_event_name/status/ts`).
     - New `CommentOut` interface: `id, event_id, text, created_at`.
     - `api.listEvents` filters gained `ticket_id?: string`.
     - New: `api.listTickets()`, `api.getTicket(id)`, `api.deleteTicket(id)` (returns `{detached_events: number}`), `api.listComments(eventId)`, `api.addComment(eventId, text)`.

   **Frontend — `admin_gui/frontend/src/lib/eventDisplay.ts`**
     - Added `describeLatestAction(name, status)`: maps a ticket's most-recent event to a human caption (e.g. "Plan approved", "Report approved", "rebuild_server succeeded", "notify_admin failed") — for the two lifecycle tools, `status==="success"` is deliberately read back as `"approved"` (since `resolve_event` overwrites a gated call's terminal status to success/error, "approved" never survives as a stored value on its own). `_STATUS_VERB` maps `pending/denied/changes_requested/error` explicitly; anything else defaults to `"approved"` (lifecycle tools) or `"succeeded"` (everything else).

   **Frontend — `admin_gui/frontend/src/lib/pendingApprovals.tsx`**
     - `decide`/`requestChanges` changed from `void`-returning to `Promise<void>`-returning (so callers can `.then(reloadTickets)` after a decision actually lands, fixing a race where reloading tickets immediately raced ahead of the backend write).

   **Frontend — new `admin_gui/frontend/src/components/TicketsGrid.tsx`** (current final state, after all iterations)
     - Imports: `ChatBubbleLeftIcon, TrashIcon` from outline; `CheckCircleIcon, ClipboardDocumentListIcon, EyeIcon, MagnifyingGlassIcon, MegaphoneIcon, WrenchScrewdriverIcon` from **solid** (per "use filled icon").
     - `STATE_ORDER = ['escalated', 'in_review', 'resolving', 'planned', 'investigating', 'completed']` — priority order, used both for section iteration and (previously) sort.
     - `STATE_LABEL`, `STATE_ICON` (one per state).
     - `STATE_COLOR` — final vibrant, all-distinct mapping: `investigating: cyan, planned: purple, resolving: yellow, in_review: pink, completed: green, escalated: red` (fixed a real dulling bug where resolving+in_review both used orange).
     - `FilterTabs`/`FilterTab` — single-select underline-tab row with inline counts, not styled as buttons.
     - `StateIcon({state})` — small colored circle+icon, used only in section headers now (removed from individual cards to avoid redundancy once sections group by state).
     - `TicketCard({ticket, onOpen, onDelete})` — current structure: title + subtitle (relative time · resource_id) + delete icon button (top); a caption strip (`describeLatestAction` text + relative time of latest event) with **neutral** `background: 'var(--color-background-muted)'` and `color="secondary"` text (fixed from the earlier state-tinted version per "it looks ugly" feedback); a bottom row with comment icon+count (`ChatBubbleLeftIcon` + `ticket.comment_count`) and `{event_count} events` on the left, and an explicit `<Link href={`/logs?ticket=${ticket.id}`}>View logs</Link>` (wrapped in a `stopPropagation` div) on the right — both restored per "bring back the comment count and deep link."
     - `sortByRecency(tickets)` — `b.id - a.id`, used within each section.
     - `StateSection({state, tickets, onOpen, onDelete})` — renders nothing if empty; otherwise a header (`StateIcon` + `Heading level={4}` label + count) followed by `<div style={{display:'grid', gridTemplateColumns:'repeat(auto-fill, minmax(260px,1fr))', gap:16}}>` of `TicketCard`s — this is the **grid-within-subsection** structure added per the "No. It's supposed to be, um, grid like" correction.
     - `TicketsGrid({tickets, onChanged})` — `activeState: string|null` (null = show all sections); `byState` grouping via `useMemo`; `visibleStates = activeState===null ? STATE_ORDER : [activeState]`; renders `FilterTabs` then maps `visibleStates` to `StateSection`s; `DeleteTicketDialog` (custom Astryx `Dialog`/`DialogHeader`/`Layout`/`LayoutContent` centered modal with Cancel/Delete buttons, replacing native `window.confirm`) rendered at the bottom.
     - Removed dead `statePriority()` helper function once sections replaced the flat sorted-list approach.

   **Frontend — `admin_gui/frontend/src/pages/DashboardPage.tsx`**
     - Removed the 4 `StatCard` stat cards entirely, removed the outer `Card` wrapper around the Tickets section (now a plain `<VStack gap={3}><Heading level={3}>Tickets</Heading><TicketsGrid .../></VStack>` directly on the page).
     - Removed unused imports (`ClockIcon, ExclamationTriangleIcon, MegaphoneIcon, ServerStackIcon, BoltIcon`, `StatCard`).
     - `handleDecide`/`handleRequestChanges` now do `decide(eventId, approved).then(reloadTickets)` / `requestChanges(...).then(reloadTickets)` instead of firing `reloadTickets()` synchronously.
     - Deleted now-fully-unused `admin_gui/frontend/src/components/StatCard.tsx` file entirely.

   **Frontend — `admin_gui/frontend/src/pages/LogsPage.tsx`**
     - Added `ticket` filter state initialized from `searchParams.get('ticket') ?? ''` (via `useSearchParams` from `react-router-dom`), `tickets` state fetched via `reloadTickets()` (hoisted function, called via `useEffect(reloadTickets, [])`).
     - `ticketOptions: SelectorOptionData[]` built from fetched tickets (`{value:'', label:'All tickets'}, {value:'unassigned', label:'Unassigned'}, ...tickets.map(t=>({value:String(t.id), label:t.title}))`).
     - `matchesTicketFilter(ticket, eventTicketId)` module-level helper.
     - `reload()`'s `api.listEvents` call and its `useEffect` deps gained `ticket`; SSE `matchesFilters` gained `matchesTicketFilter(ticket, event.ticket_id)`, effect deps gained `ticket`.
     - New `<Selector label="Ticket" options={ticketOptions} value={ticket} onChange={...} />` added to the filter panel row.
     - `handleDecide`/`handleRequestChanges` now chain `.then(reloadTickets)`.

   **Frontend — `admin_gui/frontend/src/components/EventDetailDialog.tsx`**
     - Added `TicketIcon` import from heroicons outline.
     - Added `<MetaItem icon={TicketIcon}>{event.ticket_id !== null ? `Ticket #${event.ticket_id}` : 'Unassigned'}</MetaItem>` to the meta row (alongside status Badge, duration, timestamp) — this is the "show session ID as Ticket ID" fix.

   **Frontend — new `admin_gui/frontend/src/components/CommentsDialog.tsx`** (full file, new)
     - Props: `eventId: number|null, eventLabel: string, onClose: ()=>void, onChanged: ()=>void`.
     - `useEffect` fetches `api.listComments(eventId)` on `eventId` change.
     - `submit()` calls `api.addComment(eventId, text)`, appends to local list, clears draft, calls `onChanged()`.
     - Renders via `Dialog`/`Layout`/`DialogHeader`/`LayoutContent`: list of comments (each in a `var(--color-background-muted)` block with `formatFullTime(comment.created_at)`), or "No comments yet."; error text if any; a `TextArea` (label hidden) + "Comment" `Button` (disabled if empty/sending).

   **Frontend — `admin_gui/frontend/src/components/EventTimeline.tsx`** (current final state)
     - New `CommentIndicator({count, onClick?})` — returns `null` if `count===0`; otherwise `ChatBubbleLeftIcon` + count, `stopPropagation`-wrapped click handler if `onClick` provided (interactive on real rows, display-only — no `onClick` — on the aggregate collapsed-group row).
     - `EventRow` gained required prop `onOpenComments: (event: EventOut) => void`; renders `<CommentIndicator count={event.comment_count} onClick={() => onOpenComments(event)} />` in the trailing flex area (before the Approve/Deny buttons or duration text).
     - `ReadGroupRow` gained `onOpenComments` prop (threaded to its inner `EventRow`s) and computes `totalComments = events.reduce((sum,e)=>sum+e.comment_count,0)`, rendering a non-interactive `<CommentIndicator count={totalComments} />` on the collapsed group's own header row (between the "Reading tools · N" label and the duration).
     - `EventTimeline` (exported component) gained `const [commentsEvent, setCommentsEvent] = useState<EventOut|null>(null)`; passes `onOpenComments={setCommentsEvent}` to both `EventRow` and `ReadGroupRow` call sites; renders `<CommentsDialog eventId={commentsEvent?.id ?? null} eventLabel={commentsEvent ? displayEventName(commentsEvent.name) : ''} onClose={() => setCommentsEvent(null)} onChanged={() => undefined} />` at the end of its return, self-contained (no new props needed from `LogsPage`/`DashboardPage`).

   **Tests**
   - `tests/test_investigation_reporting.py` — replaced the now-invalid `test_submit_investigation_report_never_waits_for_approval` (would hang forever now that report is gated) with `test_submit_investigation_report_waits_for_approval_then_runs` and `test_submit_investigation_report_denial_never_runs_the_handler`, mirroring the plan's existing tests.
   - `tests/test_cmp_admin_mcp.py` — `_INVESTIGATION_REPORTING_TOOLS` set gained `"start_investigate"`.
   - `tests/test_shared_db.py` — added `test_ensure_schema_creates_the_tickets_table_and_events_ticket_id_column` and `test_migration_adds_ticket_id_to_a_pre_existing_events_table` (uses named-column INSERT to avoid positional-count fragility).
   - `tests/test_admin_gui_events_router.py` — added `test_list_events_filters_by_ticket_id`, `test_approving_a_plan_event_advances_its_ticket`, `test_denying_a_plan_event_flat_escalates_its_ticket`, and (most recently) `test_new_event_has_no_comments`, `test_add_comment_and_it_shows_up_in_the_list_and_count`, `test_add_comment_on_unknown_event_is_404`, `test_list_comments_on_unknown_event_is_404`, `test_add_empty_comment_is_rejected`.
   - New `tests/test_ticket_lifecycle.py` — full unit coverage of `mcp_servers.shared.tickets` (open_ticket idempotency, current_ticket_id, backfill, `on_dispatched` bump, full `on_decision` transition matrix via `@pytest.mark.parametrize`, plus `instrument_dispatch` integration tests proving session-based auto-attribution and graceful no-session degradation).
   - New `tests/test_admin_gui_tickets_router.py` — list/get/delete coverage for the new tickets router including comment_count/event_count/latest_event fields and the soft-delete-detaches-events behavior.
   - Full suite result at last full run: **299 passed, 1 deselected** (the pre-existing, unrelated `test_real_round_trip_through_the_live_mcp_subprocess` failure, deliberately excluded via `--deselect` since it's a known issue predating this work — hits the real on-disk `guardian.db`'s saved Elasticsearch config).

4. Errors and fixes:
   - **Hung pytest process**: `test_submit_investigation_report_never_waits_for_approval` assumed report was ungated; after gating it, the test hung forever (no timeout by design). Fixed by rewriting the test to mirror the plan's approve/deny tests; killed the two orphaned `pytest.exe` processes via `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='python.exe'" | Where-Object {$_.CommandLine -like '*pytest*'}` + `Stop-Process`.
   - **`tickets.py` broke the "broken log sink never crashes a real call" guarantee**: `current_ticket_id()` called `db.connect()` with no error handling; a test monkeypatching `db.connect` to raise `OSError` now propagated through `instrument_dispatch`. Fixed by wrapping all of `tickets.py`'s DB-touching functions (except `open_ticket`, which should surface real failures) in `try/except (OSError, sqlite3.Error)` with `logger.debug` fallback, matching `telemetry.log_event`'s existing convention.
   - **"no such table: tickets" on fresh DB**: `tickets.py`'s functions never called `db.ensure_schema()` before querying, unlike `telemetry.log_event`/`log_pending_event`. Fixed by adding `db.ensure_schema()` at the start of `current_ticket_id`, `open_ticket`, `backfill_resource_id`, `_set_state`, `_close`, `_bump_if`.
   - **`start_investigate`'s own event attributed to no ticket**: because `instrument_dispatch` computes `ticket_id` once at the very top, before `dispatch()` (which creates the ticket) runs. Fixed by re-checking `current_ticket_id()` right before the final `log_event` call if the initial lookup was `None`.

"""Tests for `/api/events`: filtered/paginated listing plus the live SSE
tail.

The tail's actual push behavior is tested by driving the real
`_event_stream()` async generator directly rather than through
`TestClient.stream()`. Confirmed empirically that the latter cannot be used
at all against this route, not even to read just the response headers:
`TestClient` runs on httpx's `ASGITransport`, which drives the whole ASGI
`send`/`receive` cycle to completion before handing anything back to the
caller -- for a genuinely infinite generator (a real live tail has no
natural end), that means it hangs forever, before a single byte is
observable. This is a real limitation of this test tool against this kind
of endpoint, not a bug in the endpoint; stated plainly rather than worked
around with a fake success. SSE wire-framing itself is `sse-starlette`'s
job and isn't re-tested here.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
from datetime import UTC, datetime

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from admin_gui.backend.app import app
from admin_gui.backend.routers import events as events_router
from mcp_servers.shared import tickets
from mcp_servers.shared.telemetry import log_event, log_pending_event


@pytest.fixture
def client() -> TestClient:
    return TestClient(app)


def _log(name: str, *, server: str = "cmp-admin", status: str = "success") -> None:
    log_event(
        server=server,
        kind="tool",
        name=name,
        arguments={},
        status=status,
        error_message=None if status == "success" else "boom",
        result_summary={},
        duration_ms=1.0,
    )


def test_list_events_is_empty_by_default(client: TestClient) -> None:
    response = client.get("/api/events")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.json() == []


def test_list_events_returns_newest_first(client: TestClient) -> None:
    _log("first_call")
    _log("second_call")
    response = client.get("/api/events")
    names = [entry["name"] for entry in response.json()]
    assert names == ["second_call", "first_call"]


def test_list_events_filters_by_server_kind_status(client: TestClient) -> None:
    _log("admin_call", server="cmp-admin", status="success")
    _log("logs_call", server="cmp-logs", status="error")

    by_server = client.get("/api/events", params={"server": "cmp-logs"}).json()
    assert [e["name"] for e in by_server] == ["logs_call"]

    by_status = client.get("/api/events", params={"status": "error"}).json()
    assert [e["name"] for e in by_status] == ["logs_call"]

    by_kind = client.get("/api/events", params={"kind": "tool"}).json()
    assert len(by_kind) == 2


def test_list_events_respects_limit(client: TestClient) -> None:
    for i in range(5):
        _log(f"call_{i}")
    response = client.get("/api/events", params={"limit": 2})
    assert len(response.json()) == 2


def test_list_events_filters_by_since_and_until(client: TestClient) -> None:
    _log("before_window")
    boundary = datetime.now(UTC)
    _log("in_window")

    by_since = client.get("/api/events", params={"since": boundary.isoformat()}).json()
    assert [e["name"] for e in by_since] == ["in_window"]

    by_until = client.get("/api/events", params={"until": boundary.isoformat()}).json()
    assert [e["name"] for e in by_until] == ["before_window"]


def test_list_events_rejects_unparseable_since(client: TestClient) -> None:
    response = client.get("/api/events", params={"since": "not-a-timestamp"})
    assert response.status_code == 400


def test_list_events_since_id_only_returns_newer_rows(client: TestClient) -> None:
    _log("old_call")
    first_id = client.get("/api/events").json()[0]["id"]
    _log("new_call")

    response = client.get("/api/events", params={"since_id": first_id})
    assert [e["name"] for e in response.json()] == ["new_call"]


def test_clear_events_deletes_everything_and_reports_the_count(client: TestClient) -> None:
    _log("first_call")
    _log("second_call")

    response = client.delete("/api/events")

    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.json() == {"deleted": 2}
    assert client.get("/api/events").json() == []


def test_clear_events_on_an_empty_log_reports_zero(client: TestClient) -> None:
    response = client.delete("/api/events")

    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.json() == {"deleted": 0}


def test_approve_pending_event(client: TestClient) -> None:
    event_id = log_pending_event(server="cmp-admin", kind="tool", name="rebuild_server", arguments={})
    response = client.post(f"/api/events/{event_id}/approve")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.json() == {"status": "approved"}


def test_deny_pending_event(client: TestClient) -> None:
    event_id = log_pending_event(server="cmp-admin", kind="tool", name="delete_server", arguments={})
    response = client.post(f"/api/events/{event_id}/deny")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.json() == {"status": "denied"}


def test_decide_unknown_event_is_404(client: TestClient) -> None:
    response = client.post("/api/events/999999/approve")
    assert response.status_code == 404


def test_decide_an_already_decided_event_is_409(client: TestClient) -> None:
    event_id = log_pending_event(server="cmp-admin", kind="tool", name="rebuild_server", arguments={})
    client.post(f"/api/events/{event_id}/approve")
    response = client.post(f"/api/events/{event_id}/deny")
    assert response.status_code == 409


def test_request_changes_on_pending_event(client: TestClient) -> None:
    event_id = log_pending_event(
        server="cmp-admin", kind="tool", name="submit_investigation_plan", arguments={}
    )
    response = client.post(f"/api/events/{event_id}/request-changes", json={"comment": "try force=true instead"})
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.json() == {"status": "changes_requested"}

    row = client.get("/api/events").json()[0]
    assert row["status"] == "changes_requested"
    assert row["error_message"] == "try force=true instead"


def test_list_events_filters_by_ticket_id(client: TestClient, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setenv("CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID", "session-a")
    ticket = tickets.open_ticket("investigate something")
    _log("ticket_call")  # no session id set for this one below -- unassigned
    monkeypatch.delenv("CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID")
    _log("unassigned_call")

    monkeypatch.setenv("CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID", "session-a")
    log_event(
        server="cmp-admin", kind="tool", name="in_ticket_call", arguments={}, status="success",
        error_message=None, result_summary={}, duration_ms=1.0, ticket_id=ticket["id"],
    )

    by_ticket = client.get("/api/events", params={"ticket_id": ticket["id"]}).json()
    assert [e["name"] for e in by_ticket] == ["in_ticket_call"]

    by_unassigned = client.get("/api/events", params={"ticket_id": "unassigned"}).json()
    assert {e["name"] for e in by_unassigned} == {"ticket_call", "unassigned_call"}


def test_approving_a_plan_event_advances_its_ticket(client: TestClient, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setenv("CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID", "session-b")
    ticket = tickets.open_ticket("investigate something else")
    event_id = log_pending_event(
        server="cmp-admin", kind="tool", name="submit_investigation_plan", arguments={}, ticket_id=ticket["id"],
    )

    response = client.post(f"/api/events/{event_id}/approve")

    assert response.status_code == 200
    updated = client.get(f"/api/tickets/{ticket['id']}").json()
    assert updated["state"] == "planned"


def test_denying_a_plan_event_flat_escalates_its_ticket(client: TestClient, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setenv("CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID", "session-c")
    ticket = tickets.open_ticket("investigate a third thing")
    event_id = log_pending_event(
        server="cmp-admin", kind="tool", name="submit_investigation_plan", arguments={}, ticket_id=ticket["id"],
    )

    client.post(f"/api/events/{event_id}/deny")

    updated = client.get(f"/api/tickets/{ticket['id']}").json()
    assert updated["state"] == "escalated"


def test_request_changes_on_unknown_event_is_404(client: TestClient) -> None:
    response = client.post("/api/events/999999/request-changes", json={"comment": "nope"})
    assert response.status_code == 404


def test_request_changes_on_an_already_decided_event_is_409(client: TestClient) -> None:
    event_id = log_pending_event(server="cmp-admin", kind="tool", name="submit_investigation_plan", arguments={})
    client.post(f"/api/events/{event_id}/approve")
    response = client.post(f"/api/events/{event_id}/request-changes", json={"comment": "too late"})
    assert response.status_code == 409


def test_new_event_has_no_comments(client: TestClient) -> None:
    _log("some_call")
    event_id = client.get("/api/events").json()[0]["id"]
    assert client.get(f"/api/events/{event_id}/comments").json() == []
    assert client.get("/api/events").json()[0]["comment_count"] == 0


def test_add_comment_and_it_shows_up_in_the_list_and_count(client: TestClient) -> None:
    _log("some_call")
    event_id = client.get("/api/events").json()[0]["id"]

    response = client.post(f"/api/events/{event_id}/comments", json={"text": "checked this manually, looks fine"})
    assert response.status_code == 200
    body = response.json()
    assert body["event_id"] == event_id
    assert body["text"] == "checked this manually, looks fine"

    comments = client.get(f"/api/events/{event_id}/comments").json()
    assert [c["text"] for c in comments] == ["checked this manually, looks fine"]
    assert client.get("/api/events").json()[0]["comment_count"] == 1


def test_add_comment_on_unknown_event_is_404(client: TestClient) -> None:
    response = client.post("/api/events/999999/comments", json={"text": "x"})
    assert response.status_code == 404


def test_list_comments_on_unknown_event_is_404(client: TestClient) -> None:
    response = client.get("/api/events/999999/comments")
    assert response.status_code == 404


def test_add_empty_comment_is_rejected(client: TestClient) -> None:
    _log("some_call")
    event_id = client.get("/api/events").json()[0]["id"]
    response = client.post(f"/api/events/{event_id}/comments", json={"text": "   "})
    assert response.status_code == 400


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_event_stream_reemits_a_still_pending_row_every_tick(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setattr(events_router, "_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS", 0.01)
    log_pending_event(server="cmp-admin", kind="tool", name="rebuild_server", arguments={})

    stream = events_router._event_stream()
    first = await asyncio.wait_for(stream.__anext__(), timeout=5)
    second = await asyncio.wait_for(stream.__anext__(), timeout=5)

    assert "rebuild_server" in first["data"]
    assert "rebuild_server" in second["data"]
    assert '"status":"pending"' in first["data"].replace(" ", "")


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_event_stream_generator_pushes_a_newly_logged_event(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setattr(events_router, "_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS", 0.01)
    stream = events_router._event_stream()

    task = asyncio.create_task(stream.__anext__())
    await asyncio.sleep(0.05)  # let the generator compute last_seen and start polling
    _log("streamed_call")

    message = await asyncio.wait_for(task, timeout=5)
    assert "streamed_call" in message["data"]


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_event_stream_generator_does_not_push_events_from_before_it_started(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setattr(events_router, "_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS", 0.01)
    _log("already_existed")

    stream = events_router._event_stream()
    task = asyncio.create_task(stream.__anext__())
    await asyncio.sleep(0.05)
    _log("new_after_start")

    message = await asyncio.wait_for(task, timeout=5)
    assert "new_after_start" in message["data"]
    assert "already_existed" not in message["data"]

# Ticket-Based Investigation Tracking

## Context

Today the admin GUI's Dashboard shows Pending-approvals + 4 raw stat cards + a Servers list + Recent activity, and the Logs page is one flat, filterable timeline of every event ever logged by the three MCP servers (cmp-admin, cmp-logs, cmp-notify), via `instrument_dispatch` in `mcp_servers/shared/telemetry.py` writing to a SQLite `events` table. There's no concept of "one investigation" as a first-class thing — Plan/Report events just sit in the timeline like everything else, and there's no way to see "everything that happened during this one investigation" as a unit, or to see at a glance what's open, what needs a decision, and what's done.

This introduces **Ticket** = one investigation, with a real lifecycle (investigating → planned → resolving → in review → completed, or escalated at any point), replacing the Dashboard's current layout with a card view of tickets, and scoping the Logs page to one ticket at a time.

**Big design decision made during planning, empirically verified, not assumed:** tickets are identified by the Claude Code session id (`CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`), not by an argument the agent has to remember to pass on every tool call. I confirmed this env var is real, is set in this environment (`CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID=b809e81b-b911-4a23-823b-a40a9815ffaf` matches this exact conversation), and — critically — propagates through the exact spawn command `.mcp.json` uses for all three servers (`uv --directory cmp-mcp run python -m ...`), verified live:
```
$ uv run python -c "import os; print(os.environ.get('CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID'))"
b809e81b-b911-4a23-823b-a40a9815ffaf
```
Since all three MCP servers are spawned from the same Claude Code process for one conversation, they all see the same session id automatically. This means: **one investigation = one Claude Code session**, `start_investigate` stamps a ticket with that session's id, and every single subsequent tool call or resource read across all three servers — with no new argument, no schema change to any of the ~150 generated tools, no per-call cooperation from the agent at all — gets attributed to that ticket by a lookup inside the one shared `instrument_dispatch` function every dispatch path already funnels through. This directly satisfies the requirement that this stay "an outer layer that doesn't strictly depend on which implementation of an MCP [is calling]" — the entire mechanism lives in `mcp_servers/shared/`, untouched by any tool/resource definition.

I verified this against the real dispatch code, not just the idea:
- `mcp_servers/openapi_bridge.py:513-530` (`_register_tool_handlers._call_tool`) and `:760-792` (`_register_discovery_tool_handlers._call_tool`, the actual cmp-admin path) both funnel through `instrument_dispatch(...)`.
- `mcp_servers/openapi_bridge.py:1030-1064` (`_read_resource`) also funnels through `instrument_dispatch(..., kind="resource")`.
- `mcp_servers/cmp_notify_mcp/server.py` and `mcp_servers/cmp_logs_mcp/server.py`'s `_call_tool`s likewise call `instrument_dispatch`.

So the attribution mechanism needs exactly one new lookup inside `instrument_dispatch` itself — nothing else changes at any of these call sites.

## Ticket state machine

States: `investigating`, `planned`, `resolving`, `in_review`, `completed`, `escalated`. (Kept "Resolving" as named — it's clear; no better name found.)

| Transition | Trigger |
|---|---|
| *(new)* → `investigating` | `start_investigate` called (idempotent per session — see below) |
| `investigating` → `planned` | `submit_investigation_plan` **approved** |
| `investigating`/`planned` → `investigating` | plan **denied with a comment** (`changes_requested`) |
| any → `escalated` | plan **denied flat** (no comment) — matches SKILL.md's existing "plain no → escalate" rule |
| `planned` → `resolving` | the first `requires_approval` action tool (not plan/report/notify_admin themselves) is dispatched after the plan was approved |
| `resolving` → `in_review` | `submit_investigation_report` call becomes pending (i.e. the moment it's submitted, before any decision — mirrors how a Plan already goes "pending" immediately) |
| `in_review` → `completed` (closed) | report **approved** |
| `in_review` → `resolving` | report denied **with a comment** — admin wants more work, not just a rewrite |
| any → `escalated` (closed) | report denied **flat**, or `notify_admin` is approved and actually runs, at any point in the ticket's life |

This drops the earlier "outcome: resolved/unresolved/escalated" field idea from an earlier planning round — the state itself (`completed` vs `escalated`) already carries that meaning now that report is gated, so a separate field would be redundant. Flagging this explicitly since it reverses something discussed earlier, in case that's not what's wanted.

`submit_investigation_report` becomes approval-gated exactly like `submit_investigation_plan` already is (comment → revise → resubmit loop, flat deny → escalate) — this was foreshadowed in this project's own code comments ("later on, even the report will have accept, deny and comments") and is now in scope.

## Database (`mcp_servers/shared/db.py`)

New table, added to `_SCHEMA` (after the `events` block, ~line 55):
```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tickets (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    session_id TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    title TEXT NOT NULL,
    resource_id TEXT,
    state TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'investigating',
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
    closed_at TEXT
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_tickets_session_id ON tickets(session_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_tickets_state ON tickets(state);
```
`resource_id` starts `NULL` (unknown at `start_investigate` time) and gets backfilled the first time `submit_investigation_plan` runs for that ticket, since that's the earliest point a resource id is reliably known.

`events` gains one column, via the existing migration pattern (extend `_migrate_events_columns`, `db.py:146-152`, exactly like the prior `action` column was added — `ALTER TABLE events ADD COLUMN ticket_id INTEGER`, then `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_events_ticket_id ON events(ticket_id)` **inside** the migration function, not inside `_SCHEMA`, since `_SCHEMA`'s `executescript` runs before the migration on any pre-existing DB and would fail with "no such column" if the index were declared there instead).

No FK constraint on `events.ticket_id` — this project doesn't lean on FKs for `ALTER`-added columns elsewhere either (see `_migrate_spec_sources_columns`), and `NULL` (no ticket) is always valid, meaning historical/pre-existing events and anything called outside a session with an open ticket.

## Backend: attribution (`mcp_servers/shared/telemetry.py`, new `mcp_servers/shared/tickets.py`)

New small module `mcp_servers/shared/tickets.py` — the one place session/ticket logic lives, importable by both the MCP servers and the admin GUI backend (which already imports `mcp_servers.shared.db` directly, an established cross-import):

```python
_SESSION_ENV_VAR = "CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID"

def current_session_id() -> str | None:
    return os.environ.get(_SESSION_ENV_VAR) or None

def current_ticket_id(conn: sqlite3.Connection | None = None) -> int | None:
    """Looked up fresh on every call -- cheap indexed SELECT, always reflects
    the latest state (e.g. a ticket closing mid-session stops attributing
    further calls to it until a new one opens)."""
    session_id = current_session_id()
    if session_id is None:
        return None
    owns_conn = conn is None
    conn = conn or db.connect()
    try:
        row = conn.execute("SELECT id FROM tickets WHERE session_id = ?", (session_id,)).fetchone()
        return row["id"] if row else None
    finally:
        if owns_conn:
            conn.close()

def open_ticket(title: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Idempotent per session -- start_investigate called twice in one
    session returns the existing ticket rather than erroring or duplicating,
    since one session is always exactly one investigation."""
    session_id = current_session_id()
    if session_id is None:
        return {"error": "no_session", "message": "CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID is not set in this process's environment"}
    conn = db.connect()
    try:
        existing = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM tickets WHERE session_id = ?", (session_id,)).fetchone()
        if existing is not None:
            return dict(existing)
        cursor = conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO tickets (session_id, title, state, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, 'investigating', ?)",
            (session_id, title, db.utc_now_iso()),
        )
        conn.commit()
        return {"id": cursor.lastrowid, "session_id": session_id, "title": title, "state": "investigating"}
    finally:
        conn.close()

# --- state machine, called from both telemetry.py (pending/dispatch time)
# and admin_gui's events router (decision time) ---

def on_pending(ticket_id: int | None, name: str) -> None:
    if ticket_id is not None and name == "submit_investigation_report":
        _set_state(ticket_id, "in_review")

def on_dispatched(ticket_id: int | None, name: str, requires_approval: bool) -> None:
    """Bumps planned -> resolving on the first real action after the plan's
    approval. Only fires for genuine action tools, not the three
    ticket-lifecycle tools themselves."""
    if ticket_id is None or not requires_approval or name in _LIFECYCLE_TOOLS:
        return
    _bump_if(ticket_id, from_state="planned", to_state="resolving")

def on_decision(ticket_id: int | None, name: str, decision: str) -> None:
    """decision is one of 'approved' | 'denied' | 'changes_requested'."""
    if ticket_id is None:
        return
    if name == "submit_investigation_plan":
        {"approved": lambda: _set_state(ticket_id, "planned"),
         "changes_requested": lambda: _set_state(ticket_id, "investigating"),
         "denied": lambda: _close(ticket_id, "escalated")}[decision]()
    elif name == "submit_investigation_report":
        {"approved": lambda: _close(ticket_id, "completed"),
         "changes_requested": lambda: _set_state(ticket_id, "resolving"),
         "denied": lambda: _close(ticket_id, "escalated")}[decision]()
    elif name == "notify_admin" and decision == "approved":
        _close(ticket_id, "escalated")

def backfill_resource_id(ticket_id: int | None, resource_id: str | None) -> None: ...
```
(`_set_state`/`_close`/`_bump_if` are trivial single-row `UPDATE`s; `_LIFECYCLE_TOOLS = {"submit_investigation_plan", "submit_investigation_report", "notify_admin"}`.)

**`telemetry.py` changes:**
- `log_event`/`log_pending_event` (`:65-135`) gain a `ticket_id: int | None` parameter, added to the existing 11-column INSERT (12th column).
- `instrument_dispatch` (`:203-213`): at the top, `ticket_id = tickets.current_ticket_id()`; thread it into every `log_pending_event`/`log_event` call already inside it. Right after creating the pending row, call `tickets.on_pending(ticket_id, name)`. Right after a successful dispatch, call `tickets.on_dispatched(ticket_id, name, requires_approval)`. No caller of `instrument_dispatch` (all ~5 call sites across 3 servers + resources) needs to change at all — this is the one place all the new logic lives.

**`investigation_reporting.py` changes:**
- New `start_investigate` tool: `{"title": str}` → `required`, calls `tickets.open_ticket(title)`, **not** approval-gated (`ExtraTool(..., requires_approval=False)`, the default) — it's bookkeeping, not an infra change.
- `submit_investigation_plan`'s handler backfills `tickets.backfill_resource_id(ticket_id, arguments.get("resource_id"))` the first time it runs for a ticket (only needs `ticket_id` from `tickets.current_ticket_id()` — no schema change to the tool itself, since `ticket_id` is never an argument).
- `build_submit_investigation_report_tool()`: flip `requires_approval` to `True` (currently defaults `False` — this is the one behavioral flip that makes report mirror plan).
- Register `start_investigate` in `mcp_servers/cmp_admin_mcp/main.py::build_admin_server`'s `extra_tools=[...]`.

**Admin GUI backend (`admin_gui/backend/routers/events.py`):**
- The existing approve/deny/request-changes endpoints (already the authoritative moment a decision is made — this is what the operator's click actually calls) each gain one line: after making the existing DB update, look up the event's `name`/`ticket_id` (now stored on the row) and call `tickets.on_decision(ticket_id, name, decision)`.
- `EventOut`/`_row_to_event`: add `ticket_id: int | None`.
- `list_events`: add a `ticket_id` query param (`"unassigned"` sentinel for `IS NULL`, else numeric), same `if value is not None:` pattern already used for `server`/`kind`/`status`.

**New `admin_gui/backend/routers/tickets.py`:**
- `GET /api/tickets` — list, computed `event_count` and `comment_count` (`comment_count` = `COUNT(*)` of that ticket's events where `status = 'changes_requested'` and `name IN ('submit_investigation_plan','submit_investigation_report')` — this is the real number behind the reference UI's comment-count icon).
- `GET /api/tickets/{id}`.
- `DELETE /api/tickets/{id}` — **soft delete**: `UPDATE events SET ticket_id = NULL WHERE ticket_id = ?` then `DELETE FROM tickets WHERE id = ?`, returning `{"detached_events": N}`. Detaches rather than destroys logged evidence, consistent with this project's existing stance of never discarding logged events elsewhere (`clear_events` is the one deliberate bulk-delete escape hatch that already exists, separately). **Flagging this explicitly since it's my recommendation, not something you confirmed** — say so if you'd rather a ticket delete also purge its events.
- Wire into `admin_gui/backend/app.py` alongside the existing six routers.

## `SKILL.md` changes (`.claude/skills/investigate-incident/SKILL.md`)

Much smaller than earlier planning rounds assumed, precisely because attribution needs no per-call argument:

- **Step 1**: add one leading line — *"Before anything else, call `start_investigate` (on `cmp-admin`) with `title` set to the user's original request. Nothing else changes because of this — every later tool call and resource read in this conversation is automatically attributed to this investigation, with no extra argument to remember."*
- **Steps 2–8**: **no changes** — this is the entire point of the session-based design.
- **Step 9 (rewrite)**: `submit_investigation_report` is now gated exactly like Step 5's plan — "send and wait, no timeout" framing, plus the same revise-and-resubmit loop: a denial **with a comment** means go do more work and file a revised report; a **flat denial** is final — escalate via `notify_admin` and stop, the same way Step 6 already treats a flat denial on an execution call.

## Frontend

**Per your direction: this replaces the Dashboard's ticket area directly (no new page), a smart-sorted card grid (not columns-by-status), with a state filter control, each card showing a real progress bar and a real comment count — not decorative.**

`lib/api.ts`: new `TicketOut` type (`id, title, resource_id, state, event_count, comment_count, created_at, closed_at`), `listTickets()`, `deleteTicket(id)` (`request<{detached_events:number}>(..., {method:'DELETE'})`, matching the existing delete convention e.g. `deleteMaskingPattern`). `EventOut` gains `ticket_id: number | null`. `listEvents` filters gain `ticket_id`.

New `components/TicketsGrid.tsx`:
- **Progress bar**, derived purely from state position (real data, not decorative): `investigating` 15% → `planned` 35% → `resolving` 60% → `in_review` 85% → `completed` 100%; `escalated` renders full-width in a distinct warning color instead of the normal gradient, since it's a diverted/terminal path, not "on track."
- **Comment count**, from the backend's real `comment_count` (icon + number, matching the reference's comment-icon style).
- **Smart sort** (most-needs-attention first, per your direction): `escalated` → `in_review` → `resolving` → `planned` → `investigating` → `completed` last; ties broken by most-recently-updated first.
- **State filter**: a row of toggle chips (one per state, matching this codebase's existing `Badge`/`Button` conventions) — selecting one or more narrows the grid; default is all states.
- Clicking a card navigates to `/logs?ticket={id}` (new `useSearchParams`-based deep link, following the exact pattern `CatalogPage.tsx` already uses for `?server=`).
- A delete action per card (ghost button + `TrashIcon`, this codebase's existing pattern from `FailurePatternsPage.tsx`), gated behind `window.confirm(...)` — the one existing precedent for a confirm-gated delete in this codebase (`LogsPage.tsx`'s `clearLogs`), used here because deleting a ticket destroys its title/state/identity permanently even though its raw events survive.

`pages/DashboardPage.tsx`: remove the "Servers" `Card` panel and its `listServers()`/`listSpecSources()` fetches (nothing else on the page uses them). Keep Pending-approvals panel and Recent activity as-is. Rework the 4 stat cards to ticket counts (open/in-review/completed/escalated, computed client-side from the fetched tickets array, same style as existing `errorCount`/`avgDurationMs` derivations). Drop in `<TicketsGrid tickets={tickets} onDeleted={...} />` where the Servers panel used to be.

`pages/LogsPage.tsx`: add a `ticket` filter (`Selector` with `{value, label}` options — confirmed Astryx's `Selector` already supports object options, not just bare strings) alongside the existing Server/Kind/Status row; initialize from `?ticket=` on mount (deep link target); thread through `reload()`, its `useEffect` dependency array, and the SSE `matchesFilters` check, plus the backend's `ticket_id` param.

## Test-file risk (flagging, not rewriting up front)

`tests/test_investigation_reporting.py` (report becomes gated — `run_submit_investigation_report` is no longer called synchronously in the existing "report never waits for approval" test, that test's premise flips), `tests/test_shared_telemetry.py` (new `tickets.py` hooks called from `instrument_dispatch`), `tests/test_shared_db.py` (new table + migration test), `tests/test_admin_gui_events_router.py` (new `ticket_id` filter + decision hook), `tests/test_cmp_admin_mcp.py` (new `start_investigate` in the pinned/extra tool set). New `tests/test_ticket_lifecycle.py` recommended for the state-machine transitions end to end (no existing file owns this story).

## Verification plan

1. **Real MCP round trip**, same idiom this project's own tests already use (`mcp.shared.memory.create_connected_server_and_client_session`), against the mock CMP server (`mock/cmp_server/server.py`, already seeded with the `4a76a7df-...` incident):
   - `start_investigate({"title": "..."})`, confirm a `tickets` row appears in `investigating` state.
   - `search_logs`/`search_failure_patterns`/`admin_api_servers_retrieve` — confirm each logged `events` row has the right `ticket_id`, with **no `ticket_id` in the arguments the mock server actually received** (there's nothing to strip now, since it's never an argument — this simplifies the earlier verification concern away entirely rather than requiring a leak check).
   - `submit_investigation_plan` → approve via the admin GUI (or directly via the DB, matching how `tests/test_admin_gui_events_router.py` already drives decisions) → confirm ticket flips to `planned`, then `resolving` after the next action call.
   - `submit_investigation_report` → confirm ticket flips to `in_review` immediately, then `completed` on approval (or `escalated` on flat denial, `resolving` on changes-requested).
2. **Backend HTTP**: `GET /api/tickets`, `GET /api/events?ticket_id=<id>`, `DELETE /api/tickets/<id>`, then confirm its events reappear under `ticket_id=unassigned`.
3. **Frontend, live in the browser**: Dashboard shows the ticket card with a real progress bar matching its state, comment count matching actual `changes_requested` decisions made on it; clicking navigates to `/logs?ticket=<id>` pre-filtered; the state filter chips narrow the grid; delete removes the card and its events show up under Unassigned in Logs.
4. Full `uv run pytest` after the flagged test files are updated.

## Critical files
- `mcp_servers/shared/db.py`, new `mcp_servers/shared/tickets.py`, `mcp_servers/shared/telemetry.py`
- `mcp_servers/cmp_admin_mcp/investigation_reporting.py`, `mcp_servers/cmp_admin_mcp/main.py`
- `admin_gui/backend/routers/events.py`, new `admin_gui/backend/routers/tickets.py`, `admin_gui/backend/app.py`
- `admin_gui/frontend/src/lib/api.ts`, new `components/TicketsGrid.tsx`, `pages/DashboardPage.tsx`, `pages/LogsPage.tsx`
- `.claude/skills/investigate-incident/SKILL.md`

content.thinking:
I'm restructuring the TicketCard footer: removing the "View logs" text link, keeping event count on the bottom left, and moving the comment button plus a new deep link icon button to the bottom right.

I'm reconsidering the comment button — currently it's just a passive icon+count display with no click behavior, but the user wants it to actually be clickable, maybe opening a comments overview for that ticket. And the deep link button would just be the same navigate-to-logs action as before, but rendered as an icon button positioned bottom right alongside the comment button, rather than a text link.

Since there's no dedicated ticket-comments endpoint or dialog, clicking the comment icon probably should just navigate to the logs page too, same destination as the deep link button, with stopPropagation so it doesn't also trigger the card's own click handler.

I'll settle on: bottom left shows just the event count text, and bottom right has two elements—a comment display (chat icon plus count, kept non-interactive) and a separate icon-only deep-link button using an external-link icon that navigates to the logs page filtered by ticket id, with stopPropagation on click.

I'm reasoning that since style is merged as an inline style attribute on the root element, it should generally override the stylex utility classes due to higher specificity of inline styles, so passing custom height, padding, and color values should take effect.  The color set on the button should cascade to child spans through inheritance, overriding the ghost variant's class-based text color, while the icon's own inline color style stays separately applied and unaffected.

Now I'm working out how to shrink the button itself — overriding height, min-height, and padding inline should take precedence over the size-based classes, letting me get below the smallest predefined size while shrinking the icon to 12px and keeping the desaturated secondary color. I'll apply the same shrinking approach to the icon-only deep link button variant, using equal height and width with zero padding.

Next I'm switching the deep link button's behavior to actually copy the full ticket URL to the clipboard instead of navigating, using stopPropagation so it doesn't trigger card opening, and giving it a brief checkmark icon swap for visual feedback via a local "justCopied" state that resets after about a second and a half. I'll update the label and tooltip text to reflect the copy action, wrap the clipboard call in a light try/catch since it could fail in non-secure contexts, and then add a handful of sample comments through the API so I can visually verify the comment icons and counts render correctly.

content.subject: Step 6: resource templates incl. runbook

content.subject: Step 9: final verification pass
content.description: Full suite, ruff/format/mypy, grep for stale references, manual .mcp.json launch check.

content.subject: Step 1: Shared foundations (db/config_store/masking/telemetry)
content.description: Create mcp_servers/shared/{db,config_store,masking,telemetry}.py, SQLite schema with ensure_schema(), move masking logic from cmp_logs_mcp/mask.py to shared/masking.py with a re-export shim, add tests/conftest.py with autouse CMP_MCP_DATA_DIR tmp_path fixture. Verify full existing suite passes unchanged, ruff/mypy clean.

content.subject: Step 2: Instrumentation wiring at all 6 dispatch sites

Verify fallback/override tests, defaults unchanged when store empty.

content.description: Create admin_gui/backend/{app.py,main.py}, bind 127.0.0.1 only, health check, and routers/servers.py (list servers, tools/resources/prompts introspection via in-process builder calls, all-tools + pinned state, pin toggle endpoint). content.subject: Add LogEntry/Scorer domain types and correlate() pipeline
content.description: Create core/domain/log_correlation/ with LogEntry, ScoreContribution, RankedCandidate types and a Scorer Protocol; implement IdentifierMatchScorer and TimeWindowScorer; implement correlate(anchor, candidates, scorers) that sums contributions and ranks descending. Pure Python, no vendor deps, per the approved plan's §Architecture item 2.

content.subject: Add LogSource protocol and MockElasticsearchSource
content.description: Create integrations/elasticsearch/ with a LogSource Protocol (search(server_id, time_window, **filters) -> list[LogEntry]) and a MockElasticsearchSource that reads from registered fixture generators. Per approved plan §Architecture item 1.
content.activeForm: Building LogSource protocol and mock implementation

content.subject: Add CaseFixture protocol and 11 CSV-derived case generators
content.description: Create tests/fixtures/cmp_cases/ with a CaseFixture Protocol (generate() -> FixtureResult with signal_logs, noise_logs, expected_correlation_ids, expected_root_cause), a registry list, and one generator module per row of server create error - Trang tính1.csv (11 cases), each producing fresh random UUIDs per run plus mandatory irrelevant noise logs. Per approved plan §Architecture item 4.
content.activeForm: Building case fixture generators from the CSV

content.subject: Add mocked CMP action tool stubs
content.description: Create integrations/cmp/tools/<action>_tool/ no-op stub tools (rebuild_server, resync_volume, resync_port, etc. per the CSV's fix actions) that validate args, log what they would call, and return a fixture-defined canned result. Per approved plan §Architecture item 3 (reuses OpenSRE's existing tool registry auto-discovery, no registry changes needed).
content.activeForm: Building mocked CMP action tool stubs

content.subject: Add correlate_evidence tool wiring scorer pipeline to mock source
content.description: Expose the correlation pipeline as one tool, correlate_evidence(anchor_entry), combining MockElasticsearchSource.search() with the [IdentifierMatchScorer, TimeWindowScorer] pipeline from core/domain/log_correlation. Per approved plan.

content.subject: Write scalable test module over the fixture registry
content.description: Create tests/cmp_demo/test_known_cases.py that iterates the CaseFixture registry: generates signal+noise logs, asserts correlate_evidence returns exactly the signal set (not noise), and asserts the mocked plan/execute path calls the right no-op tool. Per approved plan's Test Module section.

content.subject: Run tests and verify the demo pipeline end-to-end
content.description: Run the new test module (and any lint/typecheck OpenSRE requires) to confirm the correlation, fixtures, and mocked tools work together as designed.
content.activeForm: Running tests to verify the demo pipeline

content.subject: Copy the 3 OpenAPI specs into the opensre repo
content.description: Copy server-spec.json, block-storage-spec.json, network-spec.json from D:\Viettel\Guardian into opensre/mcp_servers/specs/ so the MCP servers are self-contained and portable, not dependent on a path outside the repo.
content.activeForm: Copying OpenAPI specs into the repo

content.subject: Build generic OpenAPI-to-MCP bridge (parser + real HTTP client)
content.description: mcp_servers/openapi_bridge.py: parse any OpenAPI 3.1 spec into OperationSpec records (one per operationId), resolve $ref schemas from components.schemas, build MCP tool input schemas, and a CmpApiClient that makes real httpx calls (Basic or PAT auth per the spec's securitySchemes) substituting path/query params and JSON body.

content.subject: Wire mcp.server.lowlevel.Server with list_tools/call_tool
content.description: Generic build_server(name, spec_path, env_prefix) in the bridge module that registers list_tools/call_tool handlers driven by the parsed operations and a configured CmpApiClient, runnable over stdio.
content.activeForm: Wiring the low-level MCP server handlers

content.subject: Add 3 entrypoint scripts (server, block-storage, network)
content.description: mcp_servers/cmp_server_mcp/, cmp_block_storage_mcp/, cmp_network_mcp/ -- each a thin main.py calling build_server with its own spec file and env var prefix, run over stdio.

content.subject: Test the bridge against all 3 real specs using httpx MockTransport
content.description: Since no real CMP host/credentials exist, verify what's actually verifiable: parsing produces the right operation count and valid JSON schemas for all 3 specs, list_tools works, and call_tool builds the correct real HTTP request (method, URL with path params substituted, query string, JSON body, auth header) using httpx.MockTransport -- this validates the real-call logic without a live server.
content.activeForm: Testing the bridge with a mock HTTP transport

content.subject: Remap KB entries to real MCP tool names/args
content.description: Update tools/system/troubleshooting_kb/incident_patterns.json: rebuild_server entries need project_id noted (real requirement, discovered live); port_status_drift's made-up "resync_port_status" becomes the real get_elastic_ip/get_private_ip operations; volume_status_drift's verification tool becomes get_volume_legacy (the unverified legacy stopgap) since no current replacement exists -- flag that tension explicitly rather than silently downgrading the mode.
content.activeForm: Remapping KB entries to real MCP tool names

content.subject: Build generic MCP-call bridge (OpenSRE -> MCP server, stdio)
content.description: integrations/mcp_bridge/client.py: connect to a locally-spawned MCP server over stdio and call one of its tools, sync wrapper over the async mcp ClientSession -- mirrors the pattern already used in integrations/openclaw/ but generic (any command/args/cwd), not tied to one server.

content.subject: Build the dynamic OpenSRE-tool factory from MCP server + spec
content.description: Given a server launch config, a spec file, and an annotations overlay, generate one native OpenSRE @tool-wrapped function per operation (schema from the already-parsed OperationSpec, execution via the MCP bridge) and inject them into a target module's namespace so tools/registry_discovery.py's pkgutil-based auto-discovery finds them like any hand-written tool.

content.subject: Wire cmp_server_mcp as the concrete proof instance
content.description: integrations/cmp_server_mcp/tools/__init__.py uses the factory to register real tools backed by the live cmp-server MCP server; add to tools/registry_discovery.py's INTEGRATION_TOOL_PACKAGES. Block Storage and Network follow identically once this is proven.
content.activeForm: Wiring cmp_server_mcp as the proof instance

content.subject: Test the full round trip: OpenSRE tool -> real MCP subprocess -> back
content.description: A real test spawning the actual cmp_server_mcp subprocess (not just the in-process client-server helper) and calling a dynamically-generated OpenSRE tool end to end, confirming the structured not_configured error comes back correctly through the whole chain.
content.activeForm: Testing the full OpenSRE-to-MCP round trip

content.subject: Build KB signature matcher
content.description: tools/system/troubleshooting_kb/matcher.py: compile each IncidentPattern's signature_pattern template into a regex ({placeholder} -> wildcard capture), match raw error text against all patterns.

content.subject: Build router/dispatch logic
content.description: tools/system/troubleshooting_kb/router.py: run correlate_evidence, match KB via matcher, classify into designated/guided/escalate_immediately/autopilot based on mode+level reachability.

content.subject: Build Mode 1 designated executor
content.description: Constrained core.agent.Agent run limited to pattern.designated_tools, directive system prompt from pattern.instruction, CLI approval before_tool_call hook, resolved/not-resolved verdict from final text.

content.subject: Build Mode 2 guided executor
content.description: Full-tool Agent run seeded with pattern.guidance as an advisory hint in the system prompt; shares engine with Mode 3.

content.subject: Build Mode 3 autopilot executor
content.description: Broad-tool Agent run with exploratory system prompt, accepts optional prior-attempt context block from a failed Mode 1/2 run.

content.subject: Build handle_incident orchestrator
content.description: Wire router + mode executors + escalation chain (Mode 1/2 failure -> Mode 3 with carried context; escalate_immediately -> admin notify tool).

content.subject: Write fake LLM client + tests
content.description: Scripted AgentLLMClient double for tests; cover matcher, router classification (incl. core-level inert + escalate cases), Mode 1 tool restriction, Mode 2 hint injection, Mode 3 context carryover, orchestrator escalation chain.

content.subject: Run full suite, lint, update plan file
content.description: uv run pytest across affected dirs, ruff check, then mark this phase as implemented in the plan file.

content.subject: Wire requires_approval onto CMP execution tools
content.description: Set requires_approval/approval_reason on mock_rebuild_server, and compute it from HTTP method + curated annotation (via annotations_for) in integrations/mcp_bridge/tool_factory.py for the real MCP-backed tools. Probes (GET, resync_* mocks) stay ungated.

content.subject: Build plan-based CLI approval gate
content.description: Rewrite tools/system/troubleshooting_kb/approval.py: PlanRecorder (captures the LLM's stated plan via an after_provider_response hook) + cli_plan_approval_hooks (gates only requires_approval=True tools, shows the plan + args, supports y/n/edit-with-feedback that loops back to the LLM).

content.subject: Wire plan approval + instruction into all three modes
content.description: Update mode_common.run_bounded_agent to build the PlanRecorder/hooks automatically and accept input_fn/print_fn; add a shared PLAN_INSTRUCTION to Mode 1/2/3 system prompts; remove Mode 1's old bespoke gated_tools approval code.

content.subject: Update tests for the new approval flow

The DOM confirms these elements stay top-aligned side-by-side regardless of viewport width, so the bug the user is seeing must be something subtler than stacking—perhaps a mismatch in baseline alignment between the icon, count, and label elements.

Actually I recall the duration text does have paddingTop:6 applied via inline style, so the padding should push it down—but my measurement showed identical top offsets for both spans, which is confusing. I think the getBoundingClientRect on the inner text span might not reflect the wrapper's padding, so I should measure the parent element instead to see the true effective offset.

So getBoundingClientRect measures the border-box, which still starts at the same top position since padding just pushes content inward without moving the box's outer edge—meaning both elements would report identical top values even though the text glyph inside the padded box appears visually lower. That mismatch between measured box position and visible glyph position would explain the apparent vertical misalignment despite equal bounding rect tops.

Now I realize the real cause: the duration text has an intentional 6px top padding to align with the main content's first line (which itself has 4px padding on its wrapper), while the comment indicator has zero top offset, creating a visible several-pixel gap between them. There's also a horizontal misalignment—the comment badge and duration text aren't sharing a common right edge, since the comment sits further left and duration extends further right, each sized to its own natural width rather than being aligned to a shared boundary.

The fix is to wrap the comment indicator and the duration/buttons into a single flex container so they share consistent vertical alignment and a common right-aligned edge, forming one cohesive trailing meta column rather than two independently positioned elements.

Looking at the original screenshot again, the comment count and duration are already stacked vertically, so the real complaint is likely about misalignment rather than the stacking itself — the fix should just line up their right edges and top padding consistently within that same column, keeping vertical spacing uniform.

Finishing the buttons/duration column...

I need to consider the zero-comment case (indicator returns null, duration stays alone with its original top padding) and confirm this same alignment fix should only apply to EventRow, since ReadGroupRow already centers items in a single-line collapsed row and doesn't show the misalignment from the screenshot. I'll go ahead and implement the change in EventRow.
